newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shr index ends 3.28 pct lower on peso fall.
newsitem.headline: Manila shr index ends 3.28 pct lower on peso fall.

text.p: The fall of the peso to its record low and the Dow's steep drop dealt a sharp blow to Philippine shares on Monday causing the main index to post its steepest percentage drop since the peso's de facto devaluation last month, traders said.
The composite index closed lower for the eight consecutive session by 80.26 points, or 3.28 percent, at 2,368.67.
"It looked like the market was in a freefall and it's currency related, helped by the Dow's drop," said Jonathan Ravelas, head of sales at Asian Capital Equities.
Traders said the Dow's 247-point drop last Friday initially triggered the selling pressure. The selldown mounted as the peso fell to a record low of 30.14 against the dollar, they added.
The main index fell by 4.8 percent, hitting a year-low of 2,331.24 points by midsession, but recovered on a slight bout of bargain hunting in late trade.
In the broad market, losers trounced gainers 136 to four with 33 issues remaining unchanged.
Turnover was heavier at two billion pesos from the previous session's 1.37 billion.
Leading the losers were blue chip issues Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, Manila Electric Corp B, Ayala Land Inc, San Miguel Corp B and Philippine National Bank due to foreign selling.
The composite index had so far lost 332.47 points, or by 12.30 percent, from its closing of 2,701.14 points on July 11 when the peso was effectively devalued.
Traders expect the market to test the new support of 2,200 to 2,400 in the coming days.
